title: 2D scaling surface Q_S(C, n): does scaling atoms AND data jointly beat scaling either axis alone? (is the 0.2153 'ceiling' a slice artifact?)

device._note: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201; whitening and ridge on numpy CPU (M107 arithmetic); frozen encode on GPU.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.dictionary_rule: at each atom count, the prefix of the seeded permutation of the shared 8192-whitened-patch pool (seed 11) - the same rule M108/M113/M115 used, so (3072, 138000) is the sealed anchor
sparse.head: closed_form_ridge_1.0 (M108's constant, unchanged)
sparse._note: width = pool_grid^2 * atoms = 4*atoms. atoms 6144 <= 8192 pool, so all three atom counts are prefixes of the SAME random dictionary. M120 (head-width mechanism) is folded in: the atoms axis IS the head-width axis, and the per-atom Q(n) steepness is reported.

scaling.subsample_rule: first n rows of the M107-shuffled train order (nested, deterministic)
scaling.test_set: the full 34500-row shared test set, identical for every cell and atom count
scaling._note: codes are image functions, not n functions: train/test codes are encoded ONCE per atom count into D: memmaps, then a ridge is fitted at each n from the first n rows. No re-encoding per ladder point.

gate.kill_switch_superadditive: fired (fail) if the JOINT gain is not greater than the sum of the single-axis gains by the margin: at cell (1536, 34500): joint = Q(3072,69000) - Q(1536,34500); axes = [Q(3072,34500)-Q(1536,34500)] + [Q(1536,69000)-Q(1536,34500)]; super-additive iff joint > axes + 0.005. Reported: the same test at cell (3072, 69000). If atoms and data are separable resources, the 0.2153 ceiling at fixed n is a real slice, not an artifact of holding n fixed.
gate.registered_prediction: M108 measured the atoms axis at fixed n (24x atoms buys ~+10 pts, flattening); M116 measured the n axis at fixed atoms (steep, overtakes dense). If the two axes interact positively (more atoms use more data productively), the joint surface rises super-additively and the 'ceiling' was a slice artifact. If not, the ceiling is real.
